Hi Carlos,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate the context on your latency targets and the constraints the legal team surfaced around PII handling. Per our conversation I wanted to summarize the three deployment paths we discussed and propose concrete next steps so your team can pick a preferred onramp:

- Hosted API: fastest to ship; we can start with a single model and scale horizontally within our shared fleet. Good if you need to validate product fit quickly and want minimal ops burden.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with network isolation and performance SLAs; recommended if you expect sustained throughput >200 reqs/min or want predictable latency at 99th percentile.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer control, KMS/HSM integration, longer onramp due to infra and compliance validation — best for regulated PHI workloads or full data residency requirements.

Migration notes we flagged:
- Lift-and-shift from your legacy GPU cluster is feasible; we recommend a staged rollout: shadow traffic -> canary -> cutover.
- If you’re on another LLM API today, we can support side-by-side routing for a limited period to reduce risk.

Attachments: I’ve included a lightweight migration checklist (MADP-v2-migration-checklist.xlsx) and a first-pass SOW (SOW-draft-LumenHealth.pdf) for legal/ops to review.

Proposed next steps:
1) You pick preferred initial hosting mode (hosted / dedicated / private) so we can size the POC.
2) Share any blackout windows or maintenance schedules that would affect cutover.
3) If private, provide point of contact for security/compliance (we’ll need SATA/PKI/KMS contacts).

Can you confirm hosting preference by EOD Wednesday (Mar 3)? If you want, we can also schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Karthik and your infra lead to map cluster configs.

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear preference, Carlos — Dedicated makes sense for the short POC. Quick answers to your asks below and a few technical constraints to flag: 

- Dedicated capacity provisioning: For a small POC (2-4 A100-equivalent GPUs) we can provision within 7–10 business days after the signed reserved capacity PO. If you prefer a trial without commitment we can also start on Hosted with capacity reservations to approximate dedicated performance during the trial window.
- Shadowing support: yes — we provide routing controls to mirror a percentage of production traffic to the Redwood instance. Typical approach: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 10 business days, then a 2-week full shadow period before canary if you want.

Technical notes for migration from mixed legacy cluster: 
- Model artifacts: we’ll need one representative model checkpoint and a sample 4K-conversation trace to size KV cache and batching.
- Tokenization/embedding parity: if you’re using a non-standard tokenizer we’ll run a compatibility check; differences can add ~5–10% latency.
- Storage: if you choose private mode and keep model weights on-prem, we’ll coordinate a secure rsync over your private network; estimate 48–72 hours for initial sync for a 500GB model set.

Next operational step (from Redwood): I’ll draft a short runbook for the shadow-to-canary sequence and drop it in the shared Drive link. Priyom — will you push the SOW draft and checklist to the HubSpot deal?

Thanks,
